results.summary:
Partly. The left plaster hand has real anatomical masses: thenar, hypothenar, first dorsal interosseous, palm heel, dorsal wrist bump, an index knuckle dome, finger pads and a thumbnail. It holds its volume in the Blender ±35° and above views, so it is no longer the round-1 tubes or a flat card. The tone range is wide rather than one flat grey: left solid luminance p2/p50/p98 = 85/164/224 against paper at 242, and the hand alone (x>330) p5/p50/p95 = 99/172/220. The construction lines all come from the rig (wrist sections, the wrist-to-MCP metacarpal fan, the MCP ridge, bone axes, joint ticks, half-phalanx marks) or from the mesh's own outer contour. They build up in the review-B2 order during startup, and each layer overlaps the next by about 0.05 of the clock: wrist 0.2-0.3, metacarpals 0.35-0.45, knuckles 0.45-0.55, contour 0.55-0.75, solid 0.65-0.97.

It falls short of classical sculptural mass in two ways a viewer sees at the home view.

1. **Builder limit.** The form has no planes. The SDF with polynomial smooth unions gives a single smooth dome for the back of the hand. Of the knuckle row only the index dome reads. The curled middle and ring fingers are featureless round tubes, and the index has ring bulges. The drawing builds the hand from planes and angular turns.
2. **Lighting.** The forearm's shadow side is one flat dark band: 15,457 px (13% of the left hand) at luminance 81-99, std 4.0, median gradient 0. It is the darkest mass in the frame and the least modelled.

Smaller points: the 3D phalanx proportions are off (middle finger 0.89× the index, P2 shorter than P3 on the middle and ring, pinky 0.52× the index), which follows from D23 and the single-view depth reading. The thumbnail reads as a band. The reveal front shows a speckle for about 0.1-0.2 s. The forearm off-frame is a cone.

It is a smooth ramp over about 36 px (row y=215: 96 at x 260, then 103, 112, 119, 126, 128, 131, 135, 140, 145, 150 over x 264-300). results.reason:
Mostly reproduces, and I kept major, but I narrowed the finding. On my own home-view captures, the left solid's curled middle and ring fingers are smooth, even-width sausages. The drawing gives the same fingers angular PIP corners, straight-sided phalanges and DIP creases. The index shows rounded ring bulges at PIP and DIP (the 'telescoped' look). The back of the hand is one soft dome, and only the index MCP knuckle stands out clearly in the knuckle row. A viewer would notice this at the home view, and it bears directly on the 体块 (sculptural mass) question, so major holds.

Two parts are overstated or out of bounds. (1) 'No PIP knuckle turn' is too strong. In pose-left.json the middle and ring axes turn about 40 deg at the PIP in the image plane, and the render shows that bend as a soft curve with a slight outline bulge. What is missing is a crisp knuckle corner and a dorsal plane, not the turn. (2) The finding asks for planes and faceting, and calls the smooth-union builder a defect because it 'cannot produce a plane'. That runs against the documented art direction: docs/DECISIONS.md section 1 says 'Soft classical sculpture plus geometric construction lines', docs/VISUAL_V1.md section 2 says 'Soft, plaster-like solid', and review B2 says '柔和实体' (soft solid). The faceting in aes-ref/alpha-white-geom.PNG is arguably the drawing's construction-line style, which the app assigns to the line layer, not the surface. None of D1-D26 settles this, so do not treat the planes part as a settled defect. Put it to the user as a decision: should the solid carry carved planes and hard knuckle corners, or stay soft with better knuckle articulation? The defect that stands without that decision is weak articulation: tube-like curled digits, telescoped IP rings and an under-read knuckle row. The index IP rings are a consequence of D19 S4 (dorsal IP knuckles: ip_knuckle_size 0.62, k_ipk 0.01) that the decision did not foresee.

results.summary:
Partly. At the medium tier, which is the product default, the home view reads as a hand. The index finger, the two curled digits and the thumb are all legible at 1x. The thumbnail shows as a thin D loop at 3x, as D20/D21 intended. Breathing is damped near the outline: from the code and 478.5 px per world unit, the rim moves 0.7 px and the interior 2.3 px. Hover stays local (changed pixels r p95 93 px, none beyond 150 px) and recovers fully: pointerInfluence is 0.03 at 1 s, and the frame matches the baseline pixel for pixel at 4 s and 6 s. The startup gather condenses into the hand.

It does not yet read as the drawing's flowing particles (review B3):
- **The tail does not disperse.** Past the wrist the cloud is a crisp-edged tube of constant width, 116–131 px across over 0–420 px along the forearm. The drawing widens from 130 to 296 px. Only 2 of 527 tail dots lie more than 8 px outside the forearm mesh silhouette, and none more than 30 px. Around the hand, 0 dots lie outside the outline; the drawing has 51 (4.6 %).
- **The cloud is too dense, dark and uniform.** Mean ink in the hand zone is 0.167 against 0.090 in the drawing (1.86x). 10 px boxes above 0.4 ink cover 4.5 % of the zone against 0.26 %, and the biggest dark knot (2349 px) sits around the thumbnail and the curled pads. Fingertips and knuckles stand only 1.07–1.36x above the hand mean, against 1.13–2.43x in the drawing.

The D10 gate passes at the default seed (IoU 0.876–0.880) but proves less than it claims:
- It fails frames that look the same: removing 5 % of the dots at random gives IoU 0.828. Fresh seed 31337 gives IoU 0.818, contour mean 8.58, negative space 0.649. One of nine breathing phases fails the middle tip (10.0 px against 9).
- In both thinned and reseeded frames the failure comes mostly from a patch of forearm next to the wrist cut dropping out of the mask, not from the fingers.
- It passes 14 solid black blotches painted into the palm, and it passes the undispersed tail.
- It crashes with a TypeError on an empty mask instead of reporting a fail.
- It does catch a missing index tip, missing curled digits, filled finger gaps and an 8 px shift.

The low tier (6000 particles, reachable only through the dev URL) still reads as a hand at 1x. It is lighter and closer to the drawing's tone (ink 0.107), but the outline and the back of the hand break up (gate IoU 0.784, already known) and the thumbnail D is lost.

findings.title: The tail does not disperse past the wrist; the forearm is a crisp-edged band to the frame edge
findings.description: Review B3 asks for the cloud to thin out and spread past the wrist (腕后逐渐散开), and the drawing's forearm scatters widely with large free dots. The app's forearm is a straight, constant-width tube with a sharp traced rim that runs out of the frame. Cause, read from src/hand/sampling.ts: handWeight covers the whole forearm (reveal>0.04, 0.12 base + 1.2*rim^2), so the hand share traces the forearm outline all the way out. The tail share is pushed up to reach 1.1 wu (526 px) with spread 0.02+0.34 t^2 wu; the particles that would spread far also travel far and leave the frame (the wrist is about 460 px from the frame edge along the axis), so the in-frame tail barely spreads. The D10 gate cannot see this: the region past the wrist cut is in its ignore zone.

decisionsForUser: D10 (regression gate) did not foresee this: the gate's noise from reseeding, breathing phase or 5 % thinning (IoU 0.818-0.917) is as large as its margin (0.876 vs 0.85), and it mostly reacts to forearm density next to the wrist cut. It would also fail the lighter, sparser cloud that review B3 asks for. Options: (a) keep D10 as it is; (b) score the median over several seeds and phases; (c) move the cut, or score only the finger region; (d) scale the density level to the cloud's own density. Which?

Tail dispersion (review B3): the in-frame forearm is a constant-width traced band because the hand share covers the whole forearm, and the tail share mostly leaves the frame. Should the next round make the cloud disperse past the wrist like the drawing (widening to about 300 px, free dots)? That would also change what the D10 gate sees near the wrist cut.

Density and tone: the medium cloud is 1.86x the drawing's ink, with no tip/knuckle hierarchy. Reduce it in a later round (fewer or lighter hand particles, lighter rim, emphasis on tips and knuckles)? It conflicts with the D10 gate as it stands (see the first question).

results.reason: I reproduced it with my own captures and measurements. At the home view (medium and low tier) the right forearm past the wrist is a band of constant width with a crisp edge that runs to the frame edge. The dots stay within a few px of the forearm mesh silhouette. The drawing's forearm widens to roughly twice that width and scatters large free dots. Review B3 asks for exactly that: 腕后逐渐散开 (spread out gradually past the wrist). No decision D1-D26 settles the tail's form. D10 (B) only chose the regression gate. Its blindness past the wrist cut is already recorded in ACCEPTANCE.md section 7 ("The unscored zones"), so that part of the finding is known: true. The dispersion defect itself is not recorded anywhere: log-v2 line 387 defers "the tail judged against the calibrated hands" to steps 5-6. Scope: it is borderline for the question "do the particles keep the hand shape", because a crisp forearm arguably keeps the shape. But the question is framed by B3 ("reads as a hand first, then as flowing particles") and step 6 is where the tail was to be judged, so I do not refute it on scope. Major fits: it is visible at the home view in the lower-right quarter of the frame. One small numeric discrepancy that changes nothing: from the reference wrist keypoint (1282,709) at 23.4 deg, the frame edge is about 394 px along the axis, not about 460 px.

results.reason:
The finding reproduces with my own captures. At the medium tier (the default) the right-hand cloud is clearly darker and more knotted than the drawing, and you can see it at the home view at 1x. The darkest knots sit around the thumbnail and the curled pads, where the thin D is lost in the stipple. The rim is emphasised over the interior, as the reviewer says.

The reviewer's numbers run slightly high. The app's background is 242, not the drawing's paper value of 247, so the fixed PAPER constant adds a little ink. With the real background the medium tier is about 1.7x the drawing (0.150 vs 0.088), not 1.86x. The finding still stands.

It is not a decided choice reported as a defect:
- D10 (B) only set a regression gate on the particle outline and said step 6 judges whether the particles read like the drawing.
- D20/D21 decided how the thumbnail's D is traced, not how dense the cloud is.
- The 6000/12000 particle budgets and the step-4 particle tone plan are implementation, not user decisions.

It is in scope for "do the particles keep the hand shape": review B3 ("reads as a hand first") starts with exactly this complaint (粒子偏密、黑色团块明显). Major is right, because a viewer notices it at the home view. It is not a blocker: the silhouette still reads as a hand and passes the D10 gate.

I did not check the tip-density hierarchy numbers: the keypoint lookup in my script returned nothing, so that sub-claim is unverified by me.

The low tier is much closer to the drawing (0.089 vs 0.088 mean ink; few knots). That suggests a fix: lower the density or dot opacity at the default tier.

I only wrote files in my scratch folder and did not run the Playwright suite.

With my own captures, 2 of 6 fresh medium seeds fail the gate, and 1 of 3 random 10 % thinnings fails it.
